question: Should OpenClaw publish a signed standalone Android APK outside Google Play, and if so through which official channel and signing/provenance policy?
rationale: Current main has the technical ability to archive a signed third-party APK, but deciding to publish it changes the trusted Android distribution surface and signing-custody model.

options.title: Publish signed APK via current release lane
options.body: Reuse the existing Android archive/signing tooling, add maintainer-approved publication plus checksums/provenance, and document the supported install path.

options.title: Keep Google Play only
options.body: Close or narrow this request only after maintainers explicitly decide that standalone APK/F-Droid distribution is not supported and update docs to warn users accordingly.

options.title: Defer to another official channel
options.body: Choose F-Droid or another non-Play path first, then implement release automation around that channel's signing and review requirements.

recommendation.title: Publish signed APK via current release lane
recommendation.body: Reuse the existing Android archive/signing tooling, add maintainer-approved publication plus checksums/provenance, and document the supported install path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current archive, signing, Play upload, and release ref history makes this the closest available routing owner for the release-path decision.
